openings.claim: Stale exception locations cause avoidable second searches. Updating the existing behind-desk slip when a book moves may improve prompt, correct pickup for readers and reduce clerk rework; benefit remains untested.
openings.delta: Replace once-before-opening exception recording with movement-linked updates, retaining surname dividers and checking the intended reader before handoff.
openings.prediction: With current locations recorded, exception pickups show fewer second searches and fewer retrieval delays, without wrong-reader handoffs.
openings.rival_prediction: Household-surname mismatches drive the repeated searches; current exception locations alone leave those searches and delays largely unchanged.
openings.defeat: Verified current slip locations fail to reduce second searches, or updating them exceeds ten preparation minutes or increases handoff errors.
openings.probe: On a bounded evening, the sole clerk updates the existing slip on each movement and records search locations and completion times on the existing sheet. Keep all names behind the desk and use only existing shelves/cart. Time preparation, count post-opening upkeep separately, and stop preparation at ten minutes; report the 95%-within-two-minutes and zero-wrong-handoff measures.
assumptions: Fit evaluates this capped probe; sustained efficacy and ongoing update burden remain unproven.
The clerk can identify each moved hold reliably using existing private information.

openings.claim: Does the concentrated arrival interval make waiting, rather than searching, the dominant barrier to the two-minute outcome?
openings.delta: Separate waiting from retrieval before treating better storage addresses as sufficient.
openings.prediction: If queueing dominates, accurate first-location pickups still exceed two minutes mainly during the concentrated interval.
openings.rival_prediction: Retrieval errors dominate; delays follow repeated searches even outside the concentrated interval, while first-location pickups remain prompt.
openings.defeat: The concentrated interval has little waiting and nearly every late pickup spends most of its elapsed time searching.
openings.probe: Within a capped observation window, the existing clerk records encounter arrival, retrieval start and handoff on the private timing sheet. Preserve identity checks, staffing, furniture and preparation cap; classify delays without changing service priority.
assumptions: The clerk can record timestamps without materially delaying service; otherwise this probe is infeasible.
The stipulated counts do not establish actual waiting times.
